article.name: AgentRT
article.summary: AgentRT is a C11 agent runtime whose mem_d daemon stores bounded memory records in JSONL, searches by TF-IDF plus substring scoring with optional embeddings, and exposes write, retrieval, deletion, knowledge-base, cache and context-ledger APIs. This is a source review, not a runtime or performance assessment.

who_what.text: AgentRT (AirymaxAgentRT) is an OS-style C11 runtime project. Its README describes a release aggregate that pins component repositories as Git submodules. This review makes no individual-maintainer claim.

architecture.text: The release README describes a layered runtime with kernel, storage, gateway, protocol, daemon, and SDK layers. The persistent `mem_d` daemon owns memory records and exposes the `mem.*` JSON-RPC namespace; its code separates RPC handlers, service orchestration, scoped search, persistence, knowledge-base, embedding, cache, ledger, and compression modules.

A record has a generated ID, content bytes and length, optional JSON metadata, and a creation timestamp; in memory it also carries cached term-frequency vectors and optionally an embedding. The record index supports ID lookup while the service keeps records in a bounded array. The root `heapstore_memory` APIs separately account for runtime allocation pools and are not the AgentRT long-term memory API.

The daemon persists records as JSONL under the AgentRT data directory. Writes append and sync the record; delete and capacity eviction rewrite the active file through a temporary file, sync, and rename. Term vectors are rebuilt from stored text during startup load, while the external embedding service is optional.

behavior.text: Write generates a 32-character hexadecimal record ID, stores content and caller-supplied metadata, builds a TF-IDF vector, then appends the record to JSONL. When the configured record cap is reached, the oldest record is evicted. There is no general in-place update API in the inspected RPC contract; callers can write a replacement and delete the earlier ID.

Read retrieves by record ID. Delete removes the record from the active array and index, updates document frequencies, and rewrites JSONL; knowledge-base deletion removes records with the matching `kb_id`. These are hard removals from the active store, not a versioned correction or tombstone history.

Search tokenizes and scores the query against the records using TF-IDF cosine similarity fused with substring-match density (default TF-IDF weight 0.6). An optional embedding endpoint can supply vector scores; failed requests cool down and fall back to TF-IDF. The source iterates candidate records, scores them, sorts hits, and retains the requested limit. `recent` walks insertion order newest-first. `evolve` merges matching text or copies a selected record into a new record with source metadata, leaving source records in place.

Knowledge-base ingestion splits documents at UTF-8-safe byte boundaries (512 bytes by default) and writes chunks carrying `kb_id`, optional `doc_id`, and chunk index metadata. KB search filters before ranking, and KB delete removes that KB's records.

The daemon separately includes a semantic cache and a context ledger/compressor. Cache calls can report exact/semantic hits, hit rate, evictions and bytes; the append-only ledger records context composition and token counts. These are adjacent runtime facilities and should not be conflated with the persisted memory-record search result.

metrics.evidence: The source provides ranked hits and configured retrieval mechanisms, but this review ran no adjudicated answerable or unsupported probes.
No in-place correction-history contract or post-correction adjudication was established; new writes and deletes do not demonstrate stale-value performance.
The inspected deletion paths remove active records and rewrite JSONL, but no delete probes or external embedding/provider cleanup checks were run.
Search and recent accept optional conversation and tenant filters and KB search requires a KB ID. These are caller-selectable filters, not proof of authorization or isolation when omitted.
Arbitrary metadata and evolve source IDs can carry provenance-like context, but no enforced evidence validation or answer citation adjudication was identified.
The source shows linear candidate scans, full hit sorting and optional embedding network calls, but no workload timings were collected.
The ledger counts tokens and cache reports bytes, but no workload-based token, provider cost, or persistent storage measurements were taken.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of selected documentation and source at a pinned aggregate repository revision. The aggregate pins component source as submodules; no runtime, benchmark, or tests were executed, so behavior in production and any result quality remain unverified.

Default memory capacity is 1,024 records (configurable); the store is a bounded in-memory record table backed by JSONL, with vectors rebuilt on startup. Search scans the active records and sorts positive hits; the review does not establish practical scale or cost.

Conversation, tenant, and KB restrictions apply on the search/recent paths when supplied. The inspected direct get/delete methods use record IDs without scope arguments, and missing search filters leave the query broad. No authorization boundary or cross-scope leak test was assessed.

Metadata is caller-supplied JSON and is not a validated provenance ledger. Evolve records identify sources, but this review did not find an enforced source-trust policy for normal records; citation correctness, correction precedence, and multi-user safety remain unknown.
The roster entry supplied the ordinal, listed repository locator and Atlas attribution only. Atlas descriptions, marks, and layout were not used as assessment evidence.
